title: Frozen Tissue Dissociation for Single-Nucleus RNA-Seq
author: Linas Mazutis

steps.title: Prepare hood and equipment
steps.instruction: Clean the laminar hood surface and all glassware with DRNAse‑Free Reagent Spray followed by 70 % ethanol; bring an ice bucket into the hood and spray it with DRNAse‑Free Reagent; place the fully assembled Dounce homogenizer on ice to cool; bring a sterile blade into the hood.

steps.title: Prepare frozen tissue pieces
steps.instruction: On dry ice, place the frozen tissue on a Petri dish and cut it into two or three pieces roughly the size of a half‑rice grain.

steps.title: Prepare lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer 600 µL Lysis Buffer to a 1.5 mL tube, add 1.0 µL DEPC, vortex vigorously until the solution becomes cloudy and homogeneous (DEPC droplets disperse), then transfer the ready‑to‑use lysis solution into a 2 mL grinding glass tube.

steps.title: Grind tissue in glass tube
steps.instruction: Place the frozen tissue pieces in the 2 mL grinding glass tube. Using a large‑clearance pestle (Tube A), move the pestle up and down gently 10–15 times without removing it from the liquid and avoiding bubbles. Then switch to a small‑clearance pestle (Tube B) and repeat 10–15 up‑and‑down motions until the tissue is completely minced and homogenized. Keep the tube on ice.

steps.title: Record experimental observations
steps.instruction: Write down any unusual events, such as incomplete dissociation or tissue elasticity, for later reference.

steps.title: First centrifugation of lysate
steps.instruction: Place the tube (1.5 mL or 2.0 mL Protein LoBind) inside a 50 mL Falcon tube and spin in a swinging‑bucket centrifuge at 500 × g, 4 °C, for 5 minutes. Remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet (pellet should be smaller than in the previous step).

steps.title: Second centrifugation of nuclei suspension
steps.instruction: Spin the dissociated tissue suspension in a swinging‑bucket centrifuge at 500 × g, 4 °C, for 5 minutes. A clear pellet should be visible; if not, check centrifuge settings. Remove and save the supernatant, leaving approximately 10–20 µL on top of the pellet without disturbing it.

steps.title: Strain nuclei suspension through 35 µm filter
steps.instruction: Place a 5 mL Falcon round‑bottom tube with a blue Snap‑Cap strainer on ice. Strain the nuclei suspension through a 35 µm Cell Strainer Snap‑Cap into the tube. If aspiration is difficult, pour the suspension directly onto the cap, avoiding any ice on the tube walls. Transfer the filtered solution to a 1.5 mL Protein LoBind tube and keep on ice.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in wash buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL Nuclei Wash Buffer using a 1000 µL pipette.

steps.title: Resuspend and filter nuclei (optional volume)
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclei pellet in 1 mL Nuclei Wash Buffer, mixing well with a 1000 µL pipette until homogeneous (volume may be adjusted, e.g., to 0.5 mL). Filter the suspension through a 5 mL FACS Snap‑Cap strainer and collect the flow‑through.

steps.title: Evaluate nuclei with DAPI and Trypan
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL nuclei suspension with 0.2 µL 100X DAPI dye and 10 µL 0.4 % Trypan Blue dye. Inspect under bright‑field and fluorescence microscopy, record images, and expect ~10⁶–10⁷ nuclei per mL. Bright‑field shows debris; DAPI channel shows clear nuclei.

steps.title: Prepare unstained reference nuclei sample
steps.instruction: Transfer 50 µL nuclei suspension to a new 5 mL Falcon tube, add 250 µL Nuclei Resuspension Buffer, label the tube “reference” for use as an unstained FACS control, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare DAPI‑stained nuclei sample
steps.instruction: Take the remaining 950 µL nuclei suspension, add 10 µL 100X DAPI dye, mix with a 1 mL pipette, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare FACS collection tube
steps.instruction: Add 0.2 mL Nuclei Resuspension Buffer to a 5 mL Falcon tube and swirl to wet the inner walls.

steps.title: Sort DAPI‑positive nuclei on FACS
steps.instruction: Run the reference sample (step 12) on the FACS and record the scatter plot. Run the DAPI‑positive sample (step 13), identify the fluorescent population, record its scatter plot, and sort the DAPI‑positive nuclei into the collection tube prepared in step 14.

steps.title: Concentrate sorted nuclei
steps.instruction: Transfer the FACS‑sorted suspension to a 1.5 mL Protein LoBind tube and spin in a swinging‑bucket centrifuge at 600 × g, 4 °C, for 5 minutes. Adjust the final volume to achieve ~2000 nuclei/µL based on FACS counts.

steps.title: Count nuclei and assess concentration
steps.instruction: Aspirate supernatant leaving the desired volume (e.g., 200 µL), disperse nuclei by mixing with a 200 µL pipette, then mix 10 µL nuclei suspension with 0.2 µL 100X DAPI dye and 10 µL 0.4 % Trypan Blue. Count nuclei on a Countess II instrument and compare to expected results.

steps.title: Control bulk cDNA synthesis (optional)
steps.instruction: If this is the first frozen‑tissue dissociation, perform bulk cDNA synthesis and evaluate cDNA yield and profile; otherwise proceed directly to reverse transcription using the platform of choice.

steps.title: Barcoding and library preparation
steps.instruction: Follow the 10X Genomics Chromium protocol (v3.1 Chemistry) for barcoding and library preparation when using a Chromium instrument, or follow the inDrops protocol when using a home‑built inDrops platform.

steps.title: Sequence DNA library on NovaSeq
steps.instruction: Sequence the final libraries on a NovaSeq 6000 with paired‑end reads (R1 26 cycles, R2 70 cycles, index 8 cycles), targeting ~100 million reads per ~5,000 nuclei. Process FASTQ files with the SEQC pipeline, map to the reference genome using default SEQC parameters, and generate the gene‑cell count matrix.
